**LinkUp is a desktop address book for students who manage contacts across multiple projects and teams.**

It helps students organise their project mates' contact details together with relevant project information. This makes it easier to retrieve the right contact quickly and distinguish between people with identical or similar names across different projects.

- Save names, international phone numbers, emails, Telegram usernames, and an initial project.
- Allow identical names while rejecting shared phone numbers, emails, or Telegram usernames.
- Find contacts by partial name keywords or a project-name phrase.
- Associate additional projects, delete contacts by displayed index, and undo supported changes during the session.
- List all contacts, clear the address book, open command help, and exit the app.

contacts by name. Projects are added with `project`; replacing or removing a project association is not supported.

This project uses Gradle for **build automation and dependency management**. **We recommend reading [this Gradle tutorial from se-edu/guides](https://se-education.org/guides/tutorials/gradle.html).**
The following commands perform common Gradle tasks.
* **`clean`**: Deletes the files created during the previous build tasks (e.g. files in the `build` folder).
* **`shadowJar`**: Uses the Shadow plugin to create the fat JAR file `build/libs/LinkUp.jar`.
**`runShadow`**: Builds the application as a fat JAR, then runs it.
* **`checkstyleMain`**: Runs the code style check for the main code base.
**`checkstyleTest`**: Runs the code style check for the test code base.
* `./gradlew clean test`: Cleans the project before running all tests
`.github/workflows/gradle.yml` runs on pushes and pull requests, with Java 25 builds on Windows, macOS and Linux.
Each platform runs `check coverage`; Linux uses Xvfb for JavaFX tests and also runs repository-wide checks.
Codecov uploads occur on Linux using `CODECOV_TOKEN`. Check that the fork has the required Codecov configuration
before relying on its coverage badge. The separate documentation workflow deploys on pushes to `master`.
As part of CI, Gradle generates JaCoCo coverage reports from the tests, and CI uploads the coverage data to Codecov. Codecov then provides information about test coverage.

However, because Codecov is known to run into intermittent problems (e.g., report upload fails) due to issues on the Codecov service side, the CI is configured to pass even if the Codecov task failed. Therefore, developers are advised to check the code coverage levels periodically and take corrective actions if the coverage level falls below desired levels.
To enable Codecov for forks of this project, follow the steps given in [this se-edu guide](https://se-education.org/guides/tutorials/codecov.html).

The order is defined once, in `PersonNameComparator`: names are compared in lower case (`Locale.ROOT`), names
that differ only in case are ordered by their exact text, and contacts with the same name are ordered by their
saved phone value. Phone values are unique (see [Duplicate contact detection](#duplicate-contact-detection)),
so the order of any contact list is fully determined.
`SortCommand#execute` throws a `CommandException` when there are no contacts (`No contacts saved yet.`) or when
they are already in order (`Contacts are already sorted by name.`). Because `LogicManager` records an undo state
and saves only after a command succeeds, these cases change nothing and add no undo entry, matching
`edit`'s `No changes made.` handling. Otherwise it calls `Model#sortPersons`, which reaches
`UniquePersonList#sortPersons`. That uses `FXCollections.sort`, so the UI receives a single reordering change.
The filtered list keeps its predicate, so any search results stay displayed in the new order. `sort` is
undoable: `LogicManager` stores the previous address book, and `undo` restores the previous order.
* *Reorder and save the list, rather than show a sorted view (e.g. a JavaFX `SortedList`).* Indices then match
what is displayed and saved, the order survives a restart, and undo works through the existing snapshot
mechanism. The cost is that contacts added later appear at the end until the next `sort`.

The `undo` command restores the address book to the state before the most recent successful command that
supports undo and has not already been undone. It supports `add`, `edit`, `delete`, `clear`, `project`,  `deleteproject`, `replaceproject` and
Previous states are kept in a stack, so repeated `undo` commands reverse changes in reverse execution order.
When `LogicManager.execute(...)` receives a command, it checks `Command.isUndoable()`. For an undoable
command, it copies the current address book before execution. If execution succeeds, `LogicManager`
saves that copy through `Model.saveUndoState(...)`, pushing it onto `ModelManager`'s `Deque<AddressBook>`
undo history. Commands that are not undoable and commands rejected during parsing or execution will not be added
When `undo` is invoked and undo history is not empty, `LogicManager` first saves `Model.getUndoState()` to storage.
If that save fails, the contact list, filter, and history remain unchanged, allowing the user to retry.
`UndoCommand` checks `Model.canUndo()` before restoring anything. If a snapshot exists, `ModelManager.undo()`
restores the most recent snapshot with `AddressBook.resetData(...)`, removes only that snapshot from the undo
history, and updates the filtered person list to show all contacts. If no snapshot exists,
the command reports `No command to undo.`
The undo history is held only in memory and is not persisted, so it is unavailable after restarting the application.
A new undoable command after an undo adds a snapshot of the current state while preserving earlier history.
Apart from the special undo path above, `LogicManager` saves the complete address book after each command
executes successfully, including `find`, `findproject`, and `list`. Parsing and validation failures do not save.
The data path is `data/addressbook.json`, relative to the launch folder; `preferences.json` records GUI
settings. Both paths are constants in `MainApp`. Shutdown saves preferences, not a separate copy of contact data.
A failed save is reported as a `CommandException`, with a separate message for access-denied errors.
Ordinary mutations are not rolled back on disk-write failure: the UI can contain an unsaved change and its
undo snapshot. After fixing storage, a successful command such as `list` retries saving the current state.
This differs from validation failure, which leaves contacts unchanged.

CI exercises Windows, macOS and Linux with Java 25; other OS/JDK combinations are not verified by that matrix.
1.  **Environment:** The supported release setup is Windows, macOS or Linux with Java `25` installed.
2.  **Capacity:** The system shall support at least 1000 saved contacts without noticeable sluggishness during typical usage.
3.  **Performance:** The system shall return results within 2 seconds when searching using name or project for a contact list of up to 1000 contacts.
4.  **Usability:** The system shall display a clear success message or a specific error message after every command.
5.  **Interaction efficiency:** A user with above-average typing speed for regular English text should be able to complete most tasks faster using commands than using mouse interactions.
6.  **Data integrity:** If a command fails because of invalid input, an invalid index, or a duplicate, the system shall leave the contact list unchanged.
7.  **Data consistency:** The system shall validate and normalise contact and project data consistently before storing or searching it.
8.  **Persistence and reliability:** Contacts should survive restart after a successful save. An unreadable data
file is backed up before starting empty; if backup fails, startup stops with an error dialog. Ordinary save
failures report an error but may leave unsaved changes in memory, as described above.
* **Contact**: A saved record for a project mate, containing their name, contact details, and associated projects.
* **Project**: A module project or team that a contact belongs to, such as CS2103T or Orbital.
* **Project association**: A link between a contact and a project. A contact can be associated with more than one project.
* **Displayed contact list**: The contacts currently shown in LinkUp, including results of a search.
* **Index**: A one-based number identifying a contact in the currently displayed contact list.
* **Same-name disambiguation**: Using project information to distinguish contacts with identical or similar names.
* **Mainstream OS**: Windows, Linux, Unix, or macOS.

- **Consistent contact formatting.** New international phone numbers are stored without spaces or hyphens.

LinkUp is a **desktop contact manager for students working across projects and teams**. Type commands to save
contact details, associate project mates with projects, and find the right person by name or project. The contact
list shows phone numbers, emails, Telegram usernames, and projects so you can distinguish people with the same name.

contact's name, phone number, email or Telegram username, and `sort` orders contacts by name; projects are added
with `project`, removed individually with `deleteproject` and replaced individually with `replaceproject`.

### Associating an existing contact with a project: `project`
Adds one project to one or more existing contacts, preserving their other projects and contact details.
* `INDEX` is a positive integer referring to the currently displayed contact list, including search results.
* Supply exactly one `pr/PROJECT`. Project names contain 1–40 characters after surrounding whitespace

* Project comparison ignores capitalisation and normalises whitespace. For example, `Team Alpha` and
`team   alpha` refer to the same project. Adding an existing association reports an error.
* The new project is appended after existing projects. The current search filter is preserved.
* Missing or invalid indices, missing or blank project names, and repeated `pr/` prefixes are rejected.
These input errors leave contacts unchanged.

* Supply distinct positive indices separated by spaces, for example `project 1 3 5 pr/CS2103T`.

**Q**: How do I transfer my data to another computer?
**A**: Close LinkUp on both computers. Copy `data/addressbook.json` from the old launch folder into the `data`
folder in the new launch folder, backing up any existing destination file first. Launch LinkUp from that new folder.
**Q**: Why do I see sample contacts instead of my saved contacts?
**A**: LinkUp supplies sample data when it cannot find a data file at the expected path. Check the status bar and
launch it from the same folder you used previously. A different terminal folder means a different data location.
**Q**: Why does a phone number from an old file fail when I type it into `edit`?
**A**: Legacy digit-only phone numbers remain loadable, but newly entered numbers require `+` and a country code.
